citations.narrative:
The contingency plan provided was completed September 5, 2023 and only one annual review & drill was completed on
August 31, 2023. There was no documentation of said reviews or changes to the plan. The facility must review the plan
annually, document and maintain any changes or amendments to the plan.
The plan must be reviewed by the dealer, exhibitor, intermediate handler, or carrier on at least an annual basis to ensure
that it adequately addresses the criteria listed in paragraph (a) of this section. Each licensee and registrant must maintain
documentation of their annual reviews, including documenting any amendments or changes made to their plan since the
previous year's review, such as changes made as a result of recently predicted, but historically unforeseen,
circumstances (e.g., weather extremes). Contingency plans, as well as all annual review documentation, must be made
available to APHIS upon request.

Golf ball sized holes are present at the base of the entrance door jambs to the common marmoset enclosure. These holes
are found on both the left and right sides of the jamb. These holes leave the jamb in disrepair and accessible to unwanted
vermin. Facility must repair the damaged sections of the door jamb to maintain it in good repair to maintain structural
strength.
Primary enclosures must be designed and constructed of suitable materials so that they are structurally sound for the
species of nonhuman primates contained in them. They must be kept in good repair.

There are two rows of three light fixtures inside of the tiger holding building. One row on the left and one row on the right.
On the left side, the fixture at the far end of the walkway is not functioning. Two of the fixtures on the right side are also
not functioning. Functioning lights are necessary to provide sufficient illumination to view the tigers and to permit routine
inspection and cleaning. Facility must repair the fixtures to ensure proper functioning and illumination.
Indoor housing facilities shall have ample lighting, by natural or artificial means, or both, of good quality, distribution, and
duration as appropriate for the species involved. Such lighting shall be uniformly distributed and of sufficient intensity to
permit routine inspection and cleaning. Lighting of primary enclosures shall be designed to protect the animals from
excessive illumination.

The following buildings had growths of weeds and small trees inside of the gutters:
* Educational building housing regulated animals.
* The bear building housing the leopards.
*Both sides of the tiger building.
* The gutter over the viewing window of the tiger enclosure. This same gutter is sagging and is in disrepair on the right
side.
The accumulation of weeds, small trees and soil inside of gutters damage the gutters and deters the function of excess
water removal. These accumulations of plant growth must be removed to keep the gutters clean and functioning as
designed, and to reduce damage to the gutters.
Premises (buildings and grounds) shall be kept clean and in good repair in order to protect the animals from injury and to
facilitate the prescribed husbandry practices set forth in this subpart. Accumulations of trash shall be placed in designated
areas and cleared as necessary to protect the health of the animals.
This is a 1st Re-License Inspection for a Class “C” license. The inspection and exit briefing were conducted with the
applicant.
All items must be in compliance within 2 more inspection(s) or by December 6, 2026 or the applicant will forfeit the license
fee and must wait 6 months to reapply. Please contact your inspector to schedule your next Re-License Inspection.
You may appeal this finding in writing by October 16, 2026.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
Regulated activity can continue under your existing USDA license until it expires.
